newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to extend credit payments for some growers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to extend credit payments for some growers.

text.p: The Brazilian government is extending credit payment deadlines for soybeans, corn and rice producers in two states where extreme weather conditions caused crop losses this year, the Agriculture Minister said.
"We are going to authorise the extension of debt payment deadlines," Arlindo Porto said.
The extension will be valid for a maximum of two years and will be decided according to each producer's individual financial situation, he added.
"It is not automatic. It will depend on each producer's capacity to pay," Porto said.

The measure will be applied in Rio Grande do Sul where drought caused a total drop of one million tonnes in the soybean and corn harvests and in Tocantins where excess rains were responsible for a 92,000 tonne reduction in the rice crop.
The extension is subject to the approval of the National Monetary Council (CMN) which is scheduled to meet next week.

In a meeting this morning with agricultural officials, Porto also discussed simplifying credit requirements for small growers. This would include more flexibility in freeing financing currently channeled via smaller banks and signing longer-term contracts in order to reduce bureaucracy.
Porto last week announced credit for growers would increase to 8.5 billion reais ($7.94 billion) under the 1997/98 crop plan from 5.2 billion reais ($4.86 billion) the previous year.
The total cost of the new crop plan, which also has to be approved by the CMN, is estimated at 11.9 billion reais ($11.12 billion) which includes credits and investments.
